name: io.github.2016judea/ai-buildout-permits
title: AI Buildout Permits
description: US AI data-center projects from public records: tenants, air permits, turbines, resolved to tickers

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description:
Dated events on US data-center projects, newest first: Texas certifications, air-permit filings and listings, planned on-site generators, rezonings, moratoria, abatements and other city/county agenda items, and changes this ledger detected (status, tenant, delisting). Each event has its project, place, tenant or operator, tickers, the record link and a project page link. Returns the true total.

Example questions:
- "What data centers got certified in Texas this month?"
- "Which counties voted on data-center moratoria lately?"
- "Any new data-center air permits in Virginia?"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

event_type.description: certified, air_permit, rezoning, moratorium, abatement, land_use (any agenda item), generator, changes, withdrawn.

limit.description: Rows per page with a subscription (max 200).

tools.name: find_projects
tools.description:
Searches US data-center projects in the public record by state, county, city, tenant (Texas occupant), operator or permittee, any named party, ticker, status, on-site gas generation, source or name. Each row gives status, tenant, operator, resolved tickers, private parents, stated on-site MW, the record link and a page link, plus the true total of matches.

Example questions:
- "Which Texas data centers list Amazon as the tenant?"
- "Planned data centers in Loudoun County with air permits"
- "Data-center campuses with on-site gas turbines"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tenant.description: Occupant named on a certification (Texas), e.g. 'Anthropic', 'Amazon'.

operator.description: Operator, owner or permittee name, e.g. 'Microsoft', 'Vantage'.

party.description: Any named party in any role.

ticker.description: A resolved ticker, e.g. AMZN, ORCL, CRWV.

onsite_gas.description: True: only projects whose records show on-site generation.

tools.name: project_detail
tools.description:
One data-center project in full: every named party and role with its ticker link (parent, method, confidence, evidence), on-site power (technology, maker, model, unit count, MW, with the quoted source line), the dated timeline of records, coordinates where stated, and each source's publisher, URL, retrieval time and file hash. Takes a project id from another tool, or a name.

Example questions:
- "Who is behind Cipher's Barber Lake site?"
- "What turbines are permitted at Project Matador?"
- "Show the record for TX4"

project.description: Project id (e.g. tx-dc046706) or a name.

tools.name: data_centers_by_company
tools.description:
US data-center projects in the public record tied to one company, by name or ticker (e.g. 'Microsoft', 'AMZN', 'CoreWeave'): each project's status, place, role the company plays (tenant, operator, owner, permittee), stated on-site MW, record link and page link, plus the true total. Free preview of what company_exposure returns in full.

Example questions:
- "How many data centers is Oracle building?"
- "Where are Meta's data centers going up?"
- "Which projects does CoreWeave show up on?"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tools.name: data_centers_near_me
tools.description:
Data-center projects in one state, county or city from the public record: proposed, permitted, certified and operating sites, with tenant, operator, status, stated on-site MW, record link and page link, plus the true total.

Example questions:
- "Is a data center coming to my county?"
- "What data centers are planned in Loudoun County?"
- "Data centers proposed near Abilene, Texas"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tools.name: data_center_moratoriums
tools.description:
City and county agenda items that pause or ban new data centers (moratoria), newest first, with the place, the meeting date, the agenda record link and the true total. Default window: the last 30 days.

Example questions:
- "Which counties have paused data centers?"
- "Any data-center moratorium votes in Georgia?"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tools.name: data_center_zoning_votes
tools.description:
City and county agenda items on data centers: rezonings, annexations, development agreements, ordinances and other land-use votes, newest first, with the place, meeting date, record link and the true total.

Example questions:
- "Is my city council voting on a data center?"
- "Recent data-center rezonings in Ohio"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tools.name: data_center_tax_breaks
tools.description:
Tax incentives for data centers in the public record: city and county tax abatements and Texas Comptroller data-center certifications (the sales-tax exemption), newest first, with the place, tenant where stated, record link and the true total.

Example questions:
- "Which data centers got tax abatements this month?"
- "New Texas data-center tax exemptions"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tools.name: data_center_air_permits
tools.description:
Air-permit records for data centers (state DEQ and EPA ICIS-Air filings, listings and issued permits), newest first, usually for backup or on-site generators, with the project, place, record link and the true total.

Example questions:
- "New data-center air permits in Virginia"
- "Which data centers filed for generator permits lately?"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tools.name: data_centers_with_gas_power
tools.description:
Data-center projects whose records show on-site generation (gas turbines, engines), with tenant, operator, stated MW, record link and page link, plus the true total. project_detail gives the maker, model and unit count.

Example questions:
- "Which data centers are building their own gas plants?"
- "Data centers with on-site turbines in Texas"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tools.name: company_exposure
tools.description:
Every data-center project in the ledger that resolves to one ticker or company, in any role (tenant, operator, owner, permittee, equipment maker): status, place, first record date, first-seen date, stated on-site MW, plus counts by role, state and first-record year, and the link methods used. Requires a subscription.

Example questions:
- "Which data-center projects resolve to ORCL, and since when?"
- "How many Texas certifications name Amazon by year?"
- "Where does Anthropic show up as a tenant?"

ticker_or_company.description: A ticker (AMZN, CRWV, 9432.T) or a company name (Anthropic, Vantage).

tools.name: equipment_tracker
tools.description:
On-site generation at data-center campuses as the records state it: turbine or engine maker, model, unit count, unit and total MW, status and planned online date, each with its quoted source line; summarized by maker and model. Rows whose record names no maker say so. Requires a subscription.

Example questions:
- "Which turbine makers appear in data-center air permits?"
- "How many Siemens SGT-800s are permitted?"
- "Planned gas generation at data-center campuses in Texas"

maker.description: e.g. GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi, Caterpillar, Bloom.

technology.description: e.g. gas turbine, reciprocating engine, fuel cell, combined cycle.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tools.name: pipeline_series
tools.description:
Counts of data-center events or projects over time (by month, quarter or year), grouped by state, ticker, event type or source, dated by the record's own date or by first-seen date. Requires a subscription.

Example questions:
- "Texas data-center certifications per quarter since 2023"
- "Monthly moratorium and rezoning items by state this year"
- "Certifications by tenant ticker per year"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.

tools.name: export
tools.description:
A download link (valid 24 hours) for ledger rows with record dates, first-seen dates and source hashes: a CSV of events filtered by state, ticker, event type, start date or project, or the full ledger as Parquet files (events, projects, and every value each field has held with the days it was first and last seen). Requires a subscription.

Example questions:
- "Export every Texas certification with first-seen dates as CSV"
- "Give me the full ledger as Parquet for a backtest"

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX, VA, OH.
